title: spec review: C-O3 v3: `orchestrator goal start|status|list|stop` — headless goal entry point (all edits from spec reviews T-0081, T-0096, T-0097 applied)
spec:
Supersedes T-0095. Why: a goal starts today by a human opening an interactive Planner; Phase C needs a machine-callable entry point per target repo. Module orchestrator/goals.py. Contract: every public function returns a dict (or list) in every non-exceptional case; cli.py owns exit codes. goals.py reads target state only from <repo_path>/.orchestrator (tasks/*.json via json, pool.toml via tomllib, its own flock on <repo_path>/.orchestrator/bus.lock for every goals.json read-modify-write); it must not import orchestrator.bus, orchestrator.pool, orchestrator.daemon or the ROOT/STATE names from orchestrator; it may import orchestrator.install and spawn.trust_workspace only. repo_path is os.path.realpath'd once and that value is used for cwd, ORCH_ROOT and trust.
PRECHECKS (before any write): repo_path is a git toplevel with HEAD attached and no rebase/merge in progress (refuse otherwise); target pool.toml exists or install is about to create it; after install, the pool.toml has [[claude_accounts]] with id == account_id and [models].planner (refuse with {"launched": false, "reason": ...} otherwise). Add `planner = "claude-fable-5-1"` under [models] and `[secrets.planner] GH_WRITE_TOKEN = "env:GH_WRITE_TOKEN"` to this repo's pool.toml so installs carry them.
start(repo_path, goal_text, account_id="A", reinstall=False) -> dict: (a) run install.install(repo_path) when <repo_path>/.orchestrator/pool.toml is missing or reinstall=True, catching SystemExit into the dict shape; keep the report; (b) scaffold commit: paths = [.orchestrator, .claude, skills, .gitignore, .mcp.planner.json, .mcp.review.json, .mcp.scout.json, .mcp.triage.json]; run `git status --porcelain --ignored -- <paths>`; if any line is `!!` (ignored) refuse with {"launched": false, "reason": "<path> is gitignored in the target; worktrees would lack the scaffold"}; else `git add -- <exactly the paths the status output names>` and commit "orchestrator: scaffold (goal start)" with the install report lines in the body; failure → refuse; record the sha as `commit` (None when nothing to commit); (c) GOAL task: subprocess `uv run --project <this repo> python -m orchestrator.goals_create` is NOT available, so run `uv run --project <this repo> python - ` with the script on stdin and goal_text passed via env ORCH_GOAL_TEXT and repo via ORCH_ROOT (never interpolated into code), check=False; the script creates a triage task (complexity 5, acceptance ["Planner closes the goal with a PR"], scope ["**"]) and prints its id; non-zero exit or unparseable id → refuse; (d) account row → spawn.trust_workspace(account.config_dir, repo_path); env = os.environ + CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR + ORCH_ROOT=repo_path + CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the account's oauth_token_env when set + [secrets.planner] resolved by goals.py itself with the same two forms spawn uses (env:NAME, or a shell command) — implement the tiny resolver locally, do not call spawn.secrets_for_role; (e) prompt = "Skill(orchestrate) with the goal: " + goal_text + "\nThe GOAL task is " + goal_id + "; use it as the parent of every task you create and post the PR url as its result before you finish."; command = ["claude", "-p", prompt, "--model", models.planner, "--output-format", "json", "--max-budget-usd", str(limits.max_budget_usd.get("planner", 10)), "--mcp-config", ".mcp.planner.json", "--strict-mcp-config", "--append-system-prompt", <contents of .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md>, "--dangerously-skip-permissions"]; mkdir -p runs; Popen(start_new_session=True, cwd=repo_path, stdout+stderr → runs/planner-<goal_id>.log); (f) under the flock append {goal_id, repo, text, pid, pid_start (from _proc_start), started_at, account, commit, status "running", spend_counted: false} to <repo_path>/.orchestrator/runs/goals.json; return {"launched": true, goal_id, pid, log, commit, install: report, note: "goal-Planner spend is not counted against any account budget"}.
_proc_start(pid) -> epoch | None: /proc/<pid>/stat on linux, `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` with LC_ALL=C parsed "%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y" on darwin, None elsewhere. _alive(pid): three lines with os.kill(pid, 0). identity(record) = _alive(pid) and (pid_start is None or abs(_proc_start(pid) - pid_start) < 5).
status(repo_path, goal_id=None) -> list[dict]: per record: GOAL task status; children (parent == goal_id) grouped by status with hold_reason; merged shas; pr_url when the GOAL result names one; planner_alive via identity (None with a note when _proc_start is unavailable); under the flock, a record still "running" whose identity fails is marked "exited" with exited_at. list_goals(repo_path) applies the same reconciliation. stop(repo_path, goal_id): identity passes → os.killpg(os.getpgid(pid), SIGTERM), mark "stopped"; identity fails → mark "stopped" without signalling; unknown id → {"error": "unknown goal"}.
.orchestrator/prompts/planner.md = the "You are the Planner" header plus the Never and Always lists copied from CLAUDE.md, plus: "Headless: no human is in this session. When a step needs the human, write it under 'Needs the human' in plan.md and finish. The GOAL task id is given in the prompt: parent every task on it and post the PR url as its result."
cli.py: `goal start <repo> <text> [--account A] [--reinstall]` (prints the dict fields and `revert: git revert <commit>` when a commit was made; exit 2 when not launched), `goal status <repo> [id] [--json]`, `goal list <repo>` ("no goals" when empty), `goal stop <repo> <id>`; the `install` command's next-step line now points at `orchestrator goal start <target> "<goal>"`.
Tests, tests/test_goals.py, target = harness.scratch_repo (a real git repo; its .gitignore covers .orchestrator/ and .claude, which is exactly the refusal case): start_refuses_when_scaffold_paths_are_gitignored (real git, Popen patched, assert not called); start_commits_scaffold_and_records_sha (scratch repo with the ignore lines removed, real git add/commit, assert sha in return and in goals.json); start_refuses_unknown_account_and_missing_planner_model_before_any_write (no install, no commit, no task); start_creates_goal_task_via_stdin_script_with_env (subprocess.run patched: assert stdin script, env ORCH_GOAL_TEXT == text, env ORCH_ROOT == repo_path, goal_text absent from argv and script); start_launches_claude_with_expected_flags_and_env (assert --append-system-prompt with planner.md text, --strict-mcp-config, --mcp-config, goal id in the prompt, no --append-system-prompt-file, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when configured, cwd == realpath, start_new_session); start_marks_workspace_trusted; status_reconciles_exited_and_checks_pid_identity (_proc_start patched); stop_uses_killpg_only_when_identity_matches; planner_md_matches_claude_md_lists (Never/Always blocks equal). No README change (C-O5 documents the flow); no new dependency.
acceptance: tests/test_goals.py has the nine named tests and they are green; none asserts --append-system-prompt-file

goals.py imports nothing from orchestrator except install and spawn.trust_workspace (grep for 'from orchestrator' and 'import orchestrator' shows only those), and goal_text never appears inside a python -c or stdin script string (grep the source for f-strings around the script)
The launch never happens when a precheck fails, when a scaffold path is gitignored, when the commit fails, or when the GOAL-task subprocess fails; each returns launched false with a reason
pool.toml gains [models] planner and [secrets.planner]; existing pool tests green
`uv run orchestrator goal start /nonexistent x` exits 2 with one line; `goal list <scratch repo>` prints 'no goals'
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency

risks.issue: Adding top-level [models] and [secrets.planner] tables is consumed by orchestrator.pool (out of scope, not importable by goals.py per the contract). Nothing in the spec confirms Pool's TOML loader tolerates additive/unknown top-level tables. The acceptance criterion 'existing pool tests green' assumes this without a test that actually loads the new pool.toml through Pool().

goals.py takes its own flock on <repo_path>/.orchestrator/bus.lock, a path/lock scheme owned by orchestrator.bus (not importable here). This is a hardcoded-path coupling with a file outside scope: if bus.py's lock path or locking granularity changes, goals.py's RMW of goals.json silently stops coordinating with bus's own task writes, with no shared test to catch drift.

Goal-Planner subprocess spend/usage is explicitly excluded from Pool's budget accounting ('spend is not counted against any account budget'), and goals.py cannot import pool/daemon to register the account as busy. The daemon can concurrently schedule other roles onto the same Claude account while a goal-Planner is burning that account's real rate-limit window, with only a soft per-run $ cap as mitigation.

Secret resolution (env:NAME / shell-command forms) must be reimplemented locally because goals.py may not call spawn.secrets_for_role. This duplicates an unguarded external call (arbitrary shell command execution driven by pool.toml content) into a second code path, so any future security hardening of secret resolution in spawn.py must be replicated here or the two implementations drift.

The GOAL-task-creation script is passed to a subprocess as an embedded string literal that talks to orchestrator.bus's task-creation API. No import-time reference ties it to bus.py's real function signature, and the only test (start_creates_goal_task_via_stdin_script_with_env) mocks subprocess.run — a future change to bus.py's task schema could silently break real goal creation while this test keeps passing.

The acceptance criterion for injection-safety only requires grepping for f-strings around the embedded script ('none asserts --append-system-prompt-file' / 'grep the source for f-strings'). This checks one specific interpolation technique, not the actual invariant (goal_text never lands in the script text) — string concatenation or .format() could satisfy the letter of the check while still embedding untrusted goal_text into code that gets executed.

Every goals.json record carries 'spend_counted: false' but no function in this spec ever reads or flips it, and no acceptance criterion covers it — speculative schema for a feature not built in this task.

The spec says planner.md's Never/Always block is 'copied from CLAUDE.md' without naming which CLAUDE.md file (multiple exist across worktrees/repo root). The matching test (planner_md_matches_claude_md_lists) needs an unambiguous source path to be reproducible outside this worktree.

suggested_spec_changes: Add a test that loads the modified pool.toml through the real Pool() constructor/status() to prove the new [models]/[secrets.planner] tables don't break existing parsing, before relying on 'existing pool tests green.'
Either expose the bus lock path via a tiny path-only constant both bus.py and goals.py import, or add a cross-module test asserting they still agree on the lock file location.

Specify how the daemon/Pool should avoid double-scheduling an account that has a goal-Planner subprocess running against it, or explicitly document this as an accepted, human-reviewed gap rather than a silent one.

Extract the env:NAME/shell-command secret resolver into one pure, dependency-free helper importable by both spawn.py and goals.py (or amend the import-boundary rule to allow importing that one function) instead of duplicating it.
Strengthen the injection-safety acceptance criterion to assert the literal string 'goal_text' (or its value) is absent from the generated script text, not just that f-strings aren't used.
Name the exact CLAUDE.md path (e.g. repo-root CLAUDE.md relative to the orchestrator package) that planner.md and its matching test must read, so the test is reproducible regardless of worktree.
